label: pjm 49 seam hr
definition: (DIAGNOSTIC) pjm 48 coal keeper + two grounded reference-price seam corrections. (1) hr_by_year: MISO/NYISO priced per backcast year from their OWN measured realized LMP (MISO 12.38/13.92/12.03, NYISO 9.66/12.92/14.67), replacing the single 3-year-mean marginal_heat_rate that over-priced the dear-gas year. (2) Carolinas HR 13.5->11.6, reconciled to its OWN documented ~$30/MWh SERC-bilateral basis ($30/$2.54/1.02; 13.5 gave $34, +14% over, and was the highest HR of any neighbor for a cheaper region PJM net-imports from). Both rule #12 (measured/reconciled-documented > compensating estimate); forecast byte-identical. RESULT: net interchange 2023 +22.5 / 2024 +31.2 / 2025 +48.5 vs target +40/+32.7/+18 (MAE 16.5 vs 15.7 baseline); 2024 now near-perfect, Carolinas direction corrected (2024 -4.8 vs measured -6.4), gas improves 2023 (+1.9 vs +5.6) and 2025 (+10.4 vs +12.1). The MAE is marginally worse only because the fixes remove the compensating Carolinas over-export + NYISO-2023 over-price that were MASKING the real bug, now cleanly isolated: the model UNDER-clears export to MISO/NYISO (2023 MISO +17.6 vs measured +35.3, NYISO +4.3 vs +18.5) -- the $2 hurdle exceeds the ~$1.5 mean PJM-MISO spread, so the energy-spread seam can't reproduce PJM's large firm exports. Next: (1) MISO/NYISO under-export (hurdle/convex-slide), (2) add the TVA/LGEE import seam (~-8 TWh/yr), (3) anchor NYISO to the PJM-NY border not the NYC-inflated system avg, (4) 2025 EIA-930 sits ~15 TWh below PJM's per-tie sum -- a measured-source basis gap. pjm 48 stays the PJM keeper. Merged 2023-25 from parallel per-year solves. See bundle SUMMARY-seam-structure.md.
